g1|core|make-to-order|standard make-to-o.title: Make-to-Order with Production Order (Strategy 20)
g1|core|make-to-order|standard make-to-o.story: Imagine building a custom bicycle for a specific friend where no parts are made until they place their order and choose their exact color. In SAP, this is Make-to-Order (MTO) with Production Order Strategy 20, where a sales order triggers a dedicated production order holding individualized stock linked exclusively to that single customer requirement. Every component issued and labor hour posted flows directly against that sales order item's value segment. If this setup fails, the manufacturing shop floor builds generic stock instead of tailored goods, or the system blocks the delivery from picking the correct custom inventory. The process links Sales and Distribution (SD) directly to Production Planning (PP) and Finance (FI), ensuring customer-specific costs and revenues match perfectly.
g1|core|make-to-order|standard make-to-o.why_business_needs_it: Companies manufacturing specialized, engineered-to-order, or customized products need this process to isolate inventory and track exact profitability per customer project. It prevents standard inventory from satisfying custom orders and ensures production uses exact engineering parameters tied to the sales document.

g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order with.title: Make-to-Order with Assembly Processing (Strategy 82)
g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order with.story: Imagine building a custom bicycle where the moment the order is saved in the shop, the factory automatically gets the exact shopping list to build it specifically for that customer. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash (OTC), Make-to-Order with Assembly Processing uses Strategy 82 to automatically trigger production orders directly from the sales document creation, linking customer demand straight to individual stock segments. When the sales order is saved, the system creates an associated production order using requirement class 051, ensuring no standard stock is used and costs remain tied to the specific sales order item. If this integration fails, sales orders remain unconfirmed, production orders are never generated, and outbound delivery creation is blocked.
g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order with.why_business_needs_it: This process ensures customer-specific requirements trigger dedicated production runs without manual intervention between sales and manufacturing. It maintains strict cost tracking and inventory segregation for customized goods.

g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order with.title: Make-to-Order with Variant Configuration (Strategy 25)
g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order with.story: Imagine building a custom bicycle where the customer picks the frame color, gear count, and wheel size on a website, and the factory builds that exact unique bike just for them. In SAP Order-to-Cash, this means a sales order captures these custom characteristics through variant configuration, triggers a planned order and production order linked specifically to that sales order, and ensures the finished goods sit in individual customer stock until delivery. If a setting is missed, the system treats the bicycle like a standard shelf item, failing to pass the customer choices to production and mixing up the inventory. This process connects sales orders to production planning and outward shipping to deliver custom goods correctly.
g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order with.why_business_needs_it: Many customers want tailored products built to their exact specifications rather than standard off-the-shelf items. This scenario allows companies to offer endless product variations without maintaining massive finished goods inventory by configuring items dynamically during order entry and tying manufacturing directly to the sales order.

modules.role: Captures customer variant selections during order entry using sales document type OR and item category TAC, passing requirements down to planning.
modules.hands_off_to: PP (Production Planning) to trigger individual customer requirements and production orders based on strategy 25.

modules.role: Evaluates the variant configuration characteristics from the sales order, creates planned and production orders, and executes individual manufacturing.
modules.hands_off_to: MM (Materials Management) and LE (Logistics Execution) for goods receipt into individual stock and outbound delivery processing.

modules.role: Manages outbound deliveries, picking, packing, and goods issue specifically from individual customer stock segment E.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for customer billing and revenue recognition.

modules.role: Posts customer billing documents and records revenue against the specific sales order and profitability segment.
modules.hands_off_to: SD to close the order-to-cash loop.

g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order thir.title: Make-to-Order Third-Party Processing
g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order thir.story: Think of this like ordering a custom toy from a catalog where the factory tells a totally separate company to build and ship it straight to your front porch. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash, a customer places a sales order using Item Category TAS, which automatically generates a purchase requisition for an external vendor, bypassing internal warehouse stock and delivery execution while keeping the sales order linked for customer billing.
g1|core|make-to-order|make-to-order thir.why_business_needs_it: This allows businesses to offer customized or specialized products without holding inventory or investing in internal manufacturing capacity by seamlessly handing off fulfillment to external partners. It preserves single-point-of-contact customer service in OTC while automatically triggering the procurement and drop-shipment workflow.

g1|panel|make-to-order.otc_impact: Make-to-Order sits at the critical juncture where sales fulfillment meets manufacturing and external procurement, transforming standard stock-based fulfillment into highly customized, customer-specific delivery streams. In Order-to-Cash, it links inbound sales orders directly to production orders, assembly processing, variant configuration engines, or third-party vendors via requirement classes and item categories. This integration ensures that inventory allocation, pricing of configurable features, milestone billing, and revenue recognition align precisely with customized production milestones, directly protecting project margins and reducing obsolete inventory risk.

panel_qa.question: How do we choose between Strategy 20 (Production Order) and Strategy 82 (Assembly Processing) for our configured sales orders from an OTC and supply chain perspective?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Strategy 20 decouples sales order entry from production creation via manual or scheduled planning runs, allowing sales operations to capture complex requirements before committing shop floor capacity. Strategy 82 triggers an immediate production order or network creation directly upon saving the sales order via requirement class configuration, accelerating lead times for high-volume custom assemblies. We configure this in transaction OVZG by assigning the correct requirements type and checking the assembly processing indicator. The leadership value lies in balancing quote responsiveness against manufacturing schedule stability, improving on-time delivery KPIs without overloading the plant. We will review our order mix next quarter to map each product line to the optimal strategy.
panel_qa.trap: Strategy 82 is always better because it automates creation and cuts order-to-delivery lead time.

panel_qa.question: What happens to our SD pricing and condition technique when using Variant Configuration (Strategy 25) where characteristics alter the BOM and pricing dynamically?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Variant Configuration uses super BOMs and super routings where characteristics selected during sales order entry drive object dependencies that dynamically select BOM components and determine surcharge or discount conditions. We maintain variant conditions in transaction VK11 using condition tables linked to characteristic values via access sequences. When the sales order item is saved, the configuration engine passes the variant values to pricing, ensuring that customized engineering specs accurately reflect in the final customer invoice. This protects gross margins on engineered-to-order products by preventing unpriced custom features from slipping through. We are implementing standard AVC (Advanced Variant Configuration) in S/4HANA to leverage high-performance in-memory pricing.
panel_qa.trap: We just hardcode custom prices manually in the sales order pricing screen whenever a user selects a new option.

panel_qa.question: How does Make-to-Order Third-Party Processing impact our customer billing schedule, especially when goods ship directly from the vendor to our customer?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: In Make-to-Order Third-Party Processing, item category TAS or TAB automatically generates a purchase requisition linked to the sales order item, decoupling physical delivery from our internal warehouse. Customer billing can be configured for either order-related billing or invoice verification-based billing using transaction VOV7, ensuring we only bill the customer after matching vendor invoice receipt or delivery confirmation. This protects cash flow and prevents revenue leakage by ensuring supplier costs are accurately captured before customer invoicing occurs. We plan to automate the three-way match and billing release using SAP Fiori apps to accelerate our days sales outstanding.
panel_qa.trap: We bill the customer the moment the sales order is saved regardless of whether the third-party vendor has shipped the goods.

panel_qa.question: How do we prevent unverified sales orders from triggering expensive manufacturing production orders before credit or trade compliance checks are complete?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: We enforce strict credit management and trade compliance blocks at the sales order header level using SAP Credit Management (FI-CR) and SAP GTS, which prevent the requirement from passing down to PP or MM. When a sales order is blocked, the requirement type in transaction OVZG is suppressed or status management prevents MRP from generating planned orders until the block is released via transaction VKM1 or Fiori credit workspace. This avoids costly shop floor aborts and wasted raw materials for orders that ultimately fail financial clearance. Next, we are integrating automated credit scoring directly into the quotation phase.
panel_qa.trap: Production orders are automatically created immediately upon order entry and we cancel them manually if the credit check fails later.

panel_qa.question: What is the architectural mechanism linking the SD sales order item to the PP production order in Strategy 20, and how do we handle split deliveries?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The link relies on account assignment category 'M' in schedule line configuration (transaction VOV6), which sets up make-to-order stock and passes the sales order number and item number directly to the production order via requirement segment E. For split deliveries, the delivery creation splits the assigned stock from the special stock segment without breaking the production order linkage, provided that partial delivery agreements on the sales order allow it. This guarantees complete traceability from the customer invoice back to the exact manufacturing lot and raw material batch. We audit this linkage monthly via standard S/4HANA profitability segment reporting.
panel_qa.trap: We create a separate production order for every single partial delivery schedule line without regard to economic batch sizing.

panel_qa.question: How does Make-to-Order affect our period-end closing, revenue recognition, and WIP (Work in Process) reporting in Finance?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Make-to-Order often utilizes valuated sales order stock (valuation class Q) or non-valuated stock depending on costing sheet and requirements class setup in transaction OPBB. For valuated stock, production costs settle directly to the sales order item or WBS element, and revenue recognition runs via results analysis (transaction KKA1) based on percentage of completion or milestone billing. This ensures our balance sheet accurately reflects work-in-progress inventory and deferred revenue, complying with IFRS 15 standards. We will streamline the month-end batch jobs to reduce closing cycle time by four hours.
panel_qa.trap: All manufacturing costs sit in a general plant overhead cost center until the customer pays the final invoice.
